history.summary: IDENTITY CONFIRMED: Ramrekha Dham, at Kairbera about 26-28 km from Simdega headquarters, is an important Ramayana-associated pilgrimage site of Simdega district. Local belief holds that Rama, Sita and Lakshmana stayed in the hill caves here during their 14-year exile; the site's name comes from the 'Ramrekha' - lines/inscriptions on the cave ceiling that devotees believe were drawn by Rama himself. Archaeological and sacred features on site include Agni Kund, Charan Paduka (footprints), Sita Chulha (Sita's hearth) and Gupt Ganga/Gupt Gaya, with a Lakshman Kund in which pilgrims bathe on Kartik Purnima. The temple shrines of Rama, Sita, Lakshmana, Hanuman and Shiva lie inside a bowed (vaulted) cave in a scenic granite-hill setting of the Chota Nagpur Plateau. Wikipedia notes the site was discovered and developed by the Kaisalpur-Birugarh royal family (verify). A large annual mela is held every year on Kartik Purnima (October-November), drawing thousands from Jharkhand, Bihar, Odisha and Chhattisgarh. Note CSV town 'Simdega' is the district HQ; the dham itself is at Kairbera, ~26-28 km away. town_description: Simdega is a small district headquarters town in south-western Jharkhand, carved out of Gumla district on 30 April 2001. It sits amid the forested hills of the Chota Nagpur Plateau with a predominantly tribal population and is known for its hockey tradition (home to Olympic medalists). Tourist draws include Ramrekha Dham (~26 km), the Kelaghagh dam on the Chhinda river (~4 km, boating/parasailing), Ketunga Dham, and Bhairo Baba Pahari.
